A: Straight-on photograph of a real hand-finished wall panel: lime plaster tinted a warm near-black, the colour of wet charcoal with a faint brown undertone. The surface was combed by hand with a fine notched comb of about fourteen teeth: short arcing swaths, each about an arm's reach long, laid side by side and gently fanned so together they follow one long slow curve across the panel. Swaths overlap softly at their edges; small lips of pushed-up plaster sit where the comb was lifted. Between swaths are patches of flat troweled plaster with fine sand tooth, pinholes and crumbs. One low lamp at the left edge rakes across the surface almost parallel to it, so every groove throws a thin shadow, the left third glows dull bronze-grey and the right side falls away to near black. The panel fills the frame edge to edge. Photographed by Helene Binet on a Phase One IQ4 with a 120mm lens at f/11, matte, fine film grain, almost monochrome. Close: about four swaths fill the frame, every comb tooth line and sand grain readable.

F1: Straight-on photograph of a real hand-finished wall panel: lime plaster tinted a warm near-black, the colour of wet charcoal with a faint brown undertone. The surface was combed by hand with a fine notched comb of about fourteen teeth, in one single tier of tall swaths standing side by side across the whole panel. Each swath is one unbroken pull that runs from near the top edge to near the bottom edge and bends through a clear quarter-turn arc along its length; each one leans a few degrees further to the right than the one before it, so together they turn through one long slow curve from the left edge to the right edge. Every swath is a slightly different length and width from its neighbours, and their edges overlap softly. Small lips of pushed-up plaster sit only at the two ends of each swath, at a different height for every swath. Between swaths are patches of flat troweled plaster with fine sand tooth, pinholes and crumbs. A long, even band of light from far off to the left grazes the whole surface almost parallel to it, so every groove from the left edge to the right edge throws a thin shadow of the same length; the light is low and dim, the plaster stays close to black, and only the ridge tops catch a dull warm grey. The panel fills the frame edge to edge. Photographed as an architectural material study on a Phase One IQ4 with a 120mm lens at f/11, matte, fine film grain, almost monochrome. Far: the whole wall, about sixteen swaths filling the frame from edge to edge, with narrow uneven strips of flat troweled plaster between some of them; the grooves read as a fine sheen of texture on dark plaster. The light is equally dim at the left edge, the centre and the right edge, and the corners and borders of the frame are as bright as its middle.
